general: Sit or lie down and rest in a comfortable position.
Do not stay alone: ask a crewmate to stay with you and keep checking that you are responding and breathing.
A crewmate who finds you not responding and not breathing should start CPR: NASA trains crew in first aid and CPR.

chest_pain: Sit with your back supported and your knees bent, and keep still.
breathing: Check the cabin air alarms. If you think the air may be the cause, put on an oxygen mask: crew are trained to do this whenever symptoms of low oxygen appear.
fainting: If you feel faint, lie down with your legs raised, or sit with your head lowered between your knees.
Someone who has fainted and is breathing normally can be laid on their back with their legs raised.
severe_headache: Note the time it started. Tell the flight surgeon about any numbness, weakness, confusion, trouble speaking or loss of vision.
confusion: Check the cabin air alarms: low oxygen can cause mental changes that are hard to notice yourself.
Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
stroke_signs: Note the time the signs started. Stroke signs need urgent medical help even if they pass after a short time.
